name: Betaine salicylate
lead: Betaine salicylate is a salicylic acid derivative that appears in toners, serums and acne-care products, where it is used for gentle exfoliation and pore care. People use it to get clearer, smoother-looking skin with less of the stinging or dryness some experience with salicylic acid.[3]

It is a compound formed by reacting betaine with salicylic acid.[3] Salicylic acid itself is a well-known beta hydroxy acid that makes skin cells shed more readily and helps keep pores from clogging.[2] Ingredient guides describe betaine salicylate as a mild exfoliant and moisturizer, and as roughly twice as gentle as salicylic acid, so that a 4% product is described as comparable to a 2% salicylic acid one.[3] That guide adds that it is common in Korean skincare because South Korean rules limit how much pure salicylic acid formulations can contain.[3]
Published human research on betaine salicylate in skincare is very limited. A 2006 Chinese patent record describes its synthesis and proposes medicinal uses, without skincare trials.[1]

angle.text: It is used in toners and spot-care products in the way salicylic acid is, to exfoliate and reduce clogged pores. People who find salicylic acid irritating often look for it as a gentler option.

paras: Betaine salicylate is formulated into exfoliating toners and blemish-care products popular in Korean-style skincare routines. Brands position it as delivering salicylic-acid-type pore and texture benefits with a softer feel, and ingredient guides classify it as keratolytic and antimicrobial.[3]

Topical salicylic acid is used to exfoliate skin and is found in products for acne, seborrhoeic dermatitis, psoriasis, calluses and warts; cosmetic use is described as low risk, with mild skin irritation the main listed effect, and the EU restricts its use in some product types.[2]
No studies found. A 2006 patent record describes the compound's synthesis and proposes uses for it, including pain and fever relief, but it reports no skincare trials.[1]

card.summary: A gentler salicylic acid derivative used in toners to exfoliate and keep pores clear.
card.note: Few studies on this specific compound in skincare.

quick.overview:
Betaine salicylate is a salicylic acid derivative found in some toners and acne products. It is used to exfoliate gently and keep pores clear.

Users often look to it when regular salicylic acid feels too harsh.
quick.mechanism: Like salicylic acid, salicylates help skin cells shed more readily, which keeps pores from clogging. Betaine is the partner molecule in the salt.
quick.risks: Mild irritation is the main effect listed for topical salicylic acid. Human studies specific to betaine salicylate are limited.
